pll2d14c5-d1e3519.summary: Asks about the shape of heaven; the Spirit, though our authors knew, chose to say through them only what profits salvation (Augustine).

pll2d14c5-d1e3531.summary: Asks whether heaven stands or moves: if it moves, how is it a firmament; if it stands, how do fixed stars circle? It is called firmament not for standing still but for firmness or as the impassable boundary of the waters; and if it stands, nothing prevents the stars from moving (Augustine).
claims: The stars may move whether heaven moves or not.

pl-l2d14c5.summary: Asks about the shape of heaven: the Spirit, though our authors knew, chose to say only what profits salvation. Asks whether heaven moves: if it moves, how is it a firmament; if it stands, how do the stars circle? It may be called firmament for its firmness or as the impassable boundary of the waters, not for standing still; and if it stands, nothing prevents the stars from moving (Augustine).
claims: Scripture says only what profits salvation, not the shape of heaven.
'Firmament' may refer to firmness or to the boundary of waters, not immobility.
Whether heaven moves or stands, the stars can move.
